name: O'NEILL, Deborah (Deb) Mary

headline.note: Professional profile supplies St Edward’s teaching 1986–1996 and Newcastle lecturing 1996–2010. Initial school full-time status is directly described, while the university role is part-time; both sectors are excluded under the codebook. Additional Corpus Christi teaching, union governance and party roles are documented. The ABR identifies a joint Paul and Deborah Macinante partnership registered from 2000, but does not prove that it was the lawn-mowing business or establish personal work, hours or continuity. Precise transitions, leave and family-business employment arrangements remain unresolved; no public/private full-time total is supportable.

career_spells.employer: Parents' construction and plant-hire business (unidentified entity)
career_spells.role: Assisted with invoicing as a child
career_spells.evidence_note: Biographical accounts say O'Neill took responsibility for invoicing in her parents' construction and plant-hire business from about age 11. The entity, exact dates, pay, hours and legal employment status are not identified.
career_spells.counting_note: Remuneration is not documented; neither unpaid status nor a countable private full-time interval is inferred.

career_spells.employer: University of Sydney; University of New England; Australian Catholic University; Deakin University
career_spells.role: BA, Diploma of Teaching, MA and Graduate Diploma in Literacy Education student
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography lists four qualifications. O'Neill's 2013 interview describes interruption of her initial arts degree, later teacher training and a master's undertaken while teaching and raising children. Enrolment, completion dates, study loads and employment overlaps are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: In the Sisters of the Good Samaritan interview O'Neill says she was a student teacher at Mercy College, where she met her future husband. The source does not establish paid employment, dates, hours or placement conditions.
career_spells.counting_note: A student-teaching placement is treated as study unless paid employment is established.

career_spells.evidence_note: First-person 2013 interview explicitly identifies this as her first full-time job. Public professional profile now supplies 1986–1996. Exact commencement, cessation, leave and any changes from the initial full-time arrangement remain unresolved; no uninterrupted ten-year full-time tenure is inferred.
career_spells.counting_note: The source directly supports full-time status, but employment by a nongovernment Catholic school is classified nonprofit and excluded from the narrow public/private headline.

career_spells.employer: Corpus Christi College, Tuggerah (later amalgamated into St Peter’s Catholic College)
career_spells.evidence_note: The 2013 interview says O'Neill later taught at Corpus Christi College, during a period in which her three children were born. Exact appointment dates, subjects, hours, leave, career breaks and transition from St Edward's are unresolved. College history resolves the campus identity. The conference biography gives aggregate school teaching through 2000, but does not prove that this school employed her continuously until then. Its amalgamation date is not used as her cessation date.
career_spells.counting_note: Nongovernment Catholic-school employment is classified nonprofit and excluded from the narrow headline; full-time status is not assumed from the teacher title.

career_spells.employer: University of Newcastle, School of Education, Central Coast Campus
career_spells.role: Lecturer in Education; teacher-education course coordinator
career_spells.evidence_note: Professional profile supplies 1996–2010; conference biography corroborates the 2010 end year and course coordination. The 2013 interview explicitly describes part-time lecturing concurrent with school teaching, study and parenting. NTEU’s 2010 return records her occupation as lecturer. Removed election day as unsupported cessation precision. Exact FTE, breaks and transitions remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: University employment is separately classified and excluded under the current codebook; part-time work without a defensible FTE fraction would not support a full-time duration in any event.

career_spells.employer: Family lawn-mowing business (possible Paul & Deborah Macinante partnership; trading-name linkage unconfirmed)
career_spells.evidence_note: O'Neill's 2013 interview says she and her husband established a lawn-mowing business while she was teaching, studying and raising children. Member biography corroborates joint ownership; the Women’s Register also describes running a small business in its earlier candidacy account. ABR records an 'Other Partnership' jointly named Paul Joseph and Deborah Mary Macinante from 1 April 2000, active until 30 June 2026, at a Central Coast postcode. The identity and location are consistent with the spouses, but the ABR page supplies no business/trading name; it does not prove that this was the lawn-mowing business, that O'Neill personally worked throughout the registration, or her duties, revenue, remuneration, hours, leave or work boundaries.
career_spells.counting_note: Self-employment may count only when substantive full-time work and boundaries are supported; co-founding or ownership alone is insufficient.

career_spells.role: State Conference delegate and other party offices
career_spells.evidence_note: The current parliamentary biography records State Conference delegate service from 1996 and national-conference delegations in 2007 and 2009, plus undated junior vice-president and national-policy roles. Secondary synthesis reports NSW party vice-presidency from December 2011 to 2024. Remuneration, workload and exact boundaries for each office are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party organisational activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Candidate for Gosford at the NSW election
career_spells.evidence_note: ABC's 2013 Robertson guide and secondary chronology identify the unsuccessful 2003 candidacy. Nomination and election dates, remuneration, hours and overlap with teaching, lecturing and the family business are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Candidate for Terrigal at the NSW election
career_spells.evidence_note: ABC's 2013 Robertson guide and secondary chronology identify the unsuccessful 2007 candidacy. Nomination and election dates, remuneration, hours and overlap with employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: ABC reported O'Neill winning Labor preselection on 6 March 2010; the parliamentary biography records election on 21 August 2010. Campaign remuneration, hours and overlap with university or other employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Robertson
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary service history records election in 2010 and defeat at the 7 September 2013 general election.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Employment status between House defeat and Senate appointment unresolved
career_spells.evidence_note: Official service history establishes a gap after House defeat and before the NSW Parliament selected O'Neill for the Senate vacancy. Reviewed sources do not identify paid employment in this interval; absence of evidence is not coded as unemployment.
career_spells.counting_note: No sector or duration is inferred for an unresolved interval.

career_spells.role: Senator for New South Wales (casual-vacancy appointment)
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography records selection by the NSW Parliament on 13 November 2013 to replace Bob Carr and service through 30 June 2014.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The parliamentary biography records a renewed NSW parliamentary choice on 2 July 2014, election to the Senate in 2016 and re-election in 2022; service was current at the frozen snapshot.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Named in the union’s statutory 2010 return, alongside lecturer occupation. Exact term, remuneration and hours are unknown; not assumed to be paid union staff.

research_notes: Blocked pending exact dates, subjects, hours, leave and career breaks for St Edward's and Corpus Christi teaching, including whether any other school employers are omitted.

Obtain University of Newcastle appointment records, title progression, campus/school, start and cessation dates, FTE fraction, leave and overlap with teaching, study, business and campaigns.
Identify the lawn-mowing business entity, dates, ownership, duties, customers, remuneration, hours, leave and whether it continued through candidacies or federal service.
Determine remuneration and workload for ALP offices and the 2003, 2007 and 2010 campaigns; identify any paid work in the September–November 2013 parliamentary gap.

No public/private full-time duration is inferred from the generic teacher/lecturer labels. The directly described full-time St Edward's role remains a nonprofit exclusion; missing evidence is not zero.

2026-10-01 follow-up: added publicly indexed professional-profile years, conference biography, statutory NTEU office, school history and additional party roles. Corrected election-day university cessation precision and unsupported unpaid classification of childhood family assistance.

Overall school range 1986–2000 in the 2017 conference biography extends beyond the St Edward’s 1986–1996 profile entry; preserve later Corpus Christi teaching and possible overlap with part-time Newcastle work rather than force a sequential full-time timeline. Exact school transfer and leave remain gaps.

Searched Newcastle institutional pages, school chronology, professional profile, conference biographies, statutory union records and small-business references including spouse name. Direct LinkedIn and Good Samaritan pages returned retrieval errors; public profile search indexing supplied explicit years. No business entity or full-time labour evidence found. Generic university profile and music-teacher namesakes excluded.

Second follow-up2October2026: targeted Corpus Christi transfer-year, ACU/Deakin graduation, Newcastle casual/part-time and family lawn-business searches found no supported new employment boundaries, hours or legal entity. Reviewed public indexing of the existing2013 Good Samaritan interview and current member biography; neither resolves these gaps. A public Brenden Wood recollection identifies a former teacher as Miss Macinante and now Senator O’Neill (https://www.facebook.com/BrendenWood/posts/today-we-bumped-into-a-high-school-teacher-that-i-hadnt-seen-for-36-years-miss-m/10158593970496741/); retain only as an archival name-variant lead, not independently established dates or subjects. Searches under Deborah/Deb Macinante and spouse Paul did not identify school payroll or business records. Stirling academic, Irish music teacher and American federal employee are namesakes excluded. Next useful avenues: school staff/yearbook archives under both surnames, university appointment/leave records and original business records. Exhausted broad queries should not be repeated without a new lead. No career facts or totals changed.

Third follow-up3October2026: searching the Macinante archival surname produced ABR 79 527 309 834, an Other Partnership jointly named for Paul Joseph and Deborah Mary Macinante, registered from 1April2000 and cancelled30June2026 at NSW2251. This materially narrows the possible legal form and outer registration window of the jointly owned business. The registry page gives no business name, so the lawn-mowing linkage, actual operating dates, personal labour, pay and hours remain unproved; registration is not converted into an employment interval.

Fourth follow-up4October2026 used exact ABN, joint-name and lawn-mowing/business queries. Results did not reveal a trading name, operating activity, customer record or personal work evidence; unrelated family and namesake material was excluded. The partnership remains only a possible legal-form lead and is not converted into a lawn-business or employment spell.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Targeted school staff/yearbook indexing under Deborah/Deb Macinante and O’Neill yielded no dated teaching appointment, subject allocation, Corpus Christi transfer, leave or workload record. Unrelated Perth Corpus Christi/St Joseph’s school results were excluded: her recorded college is Tuggerah. NSW public-school staff lists concern other people and do not establish a public-school job. Both search engines primarily returned previously recorded biographies or copies. Preserve nonprofit school classification and supported initial full-time status without extending continuity; family partnership linkage remains unconfirmed. Next useful evidence is an original school staff archive or university appointment/leave record; do not repeat exhausted broad surname searches.

Follow-up2026-10-05: Targeted Newcastle course/handbook indexing for 1997/1999 and the Macinante surname, checked with both engines, yielded existing biography/profile material and unrelated Irish/US teaching namesakes. No appointment, FTE, leave or school-transfer record. A St Patricks College alumni-story index describes Senator Deborah ONeill as Class of1978 (https://saintpatricks.nsw.edu.au/alumni-stories-doneill/), but original open returned403 Forbidden; retain as a school-archive lead, not a university graduation, job or inferred employment boundary. Tasmanian unclaimed-money indexing names the Macinante partnership but does not establish lawn-business activity, paid personal labour or working dates. No supported employment fact changed. Original Newcastle personnel/course archive and contemporaneous school staff records remain the useful next avenues.

Second targeted primary pass2026-10-05: Followed Newcastle course-coordinator/publication and Macinante surname routes, then new original FWC Newcastle-branch NTEU financial filings for2002,2007 and2008: https://regorgs.fwc.gov.au/sites/default/files/migration/393/283vnewc-fr2002-462.pdf ; https://regorgs.fwc.gov.au/sites/default/files/migration/393/283vnewc-fr2007-343.pdf ; https://regorgs.fwc.gov.au/sites/default/files/migration/393/283vnewc-fr2008-423.pdf . Readable report text contains no Neill match; cannot use branch-wide expenditure, officeholders or filing-year ranges as her individual pay, union tenure or university FTE. Namesakes Deborah Hodgson/Trevallion/Chambers/Ralls and modern graduation story excluded. Primary course/staff allocation or original university appointment/leave records remain the useful next evidence; school-transfer and business-labour gaps preserved. No new attributable employment fact or headline duration.

Third targeted pass2026-10-06: Re-ran exact Fair Work registered-organisation, University of Newcastle and Macinante surname searches. The FWC search returned the already held26July2010 NTEU return listing O’Neill as lecturer and Newcastle branch committee member; later annual-return/election material concerned different people. University results identify her only retrospectively as former staff or in elected-office appearances, not a teaching appointment, FTE, leave or cessation record. ABR results repeat the joint partnership name history without a business name or labour evidence. No personal employment term changed; these routes are exhausted pending a primary university personnel/course allocation, school staff record or business trading-name document.
